title: Uri language — Grokipedia
text: The numeral system of Uri, a Trans-New Guinea language spoken in Morobe Province, Papua New Guinea, is a digit-tally based structure that relies on a small set of basic terms for 1, 2, and 3, with higher numbers formed through additive compounds.

text: Uri is an endangered indigenous language of Papua New Guinea. It belongs to the Trans-New Guinea language family. The language is used as a first language by all adults in the ethnic community, but not all young people. It is not known to be taught in schools.
